newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-BROADHURST MOVES UP TO SHARE LEAD WITH ROCCA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BROADHURST MOVES UP TO SHARE LEAD WITH ROCCA.

text.p: Paul Broadhurst, chasing his first win since last year's French Open, surprised even himself when he fired a 68 to share the lead with Italian Costantino Rocca in the European Open on Saturday.
The Briton, one stroke behind Rocca at the halfway stage, was far from optimistic when he began the third round.

"I hit the ball so badly on the range before I went out I didn't know what to expect. I was cutting it, then I would pull one. It was just a mixed bag, I don't think I hit two shots the same," he said.
But once on the course, everything went right and his four under par 68 took him level on 206 with Rocca who had a 69.
"I suppose that's golf. Probably tomorrow I'll hit it well on the range and play badly," Broadhurst said.
He almost had two eagles. His 75-yard pitch to the par five first stopped only inches away and on the 413-yard 11th his nine iron approach did the same.
Rocca, joint halfway leader with Jim Payne, jumped into a two-shot lead with three birdies in his first four holes but allowed the chasing pack to catch him with bogeys at the fifth and eighth.
Sweden's Per-Ulrik Johansson moved into third place only a shot behind with a 66, while Scotland's Andrew Coltart was alone in fourth on eight under after a 69.
Payne managed only a 72 to drop into a share of fifth spot with Ireland's Padraig Harrington, Spaniard Miguel Angel Martin and Briton Derrick Cooper.

Colin Montgomerie, although 11 off the pace after a 70, still moved closer to winning his fourth European Order of Merit. Fellow Briton and closest rival Ian Woosnam fell even further back with a 74 which left him four over par and three behind Montgomerie.
